territorial_scope.description: Applies to exports from the United States, and to reexports and in-country transfers of items subject to the EAR, for end-users or destinations in China and Macau.

summary.short: BIS final rule, effective 15 January 2026, moves licence review for exports to China or Macau of certain advanced AI chips (TPP below 21,000, total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s) from a presumption of denial to case-by-case review, conditional on exporter certifications and independent third-party testing.
summary.long: Final rule by the Bureau of Industry and Security amending the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR parts 742, 744 and 748), effective 15 January 2026. For exports from the United States of advanced computing commodities with a TPP below 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s destined to end-users in China or Macau, § 742.6(b)(10)(iii)(A)(1) replaces the presumption of denial with case-by-case review, if the applicant submits the certifications in Supplement No. 2 to Part 748, paragraph (dd). Certifications cover units shipped in the United States, sufficient US supply, no diversion of foundry capacity, aggregate shipments to China and Macau no more than 50 percent of US end-use shipments, exclusion of military and WMD end uses, Know Your Customer procedures, a list of IaaS remote end users in listed countries, physical security, and review of each shipment by a US-based independent third-party testing lab. BIS may revoke a lab's qualification, which suspends the policy for exporters using it. The presumption of denial continues for Macau, Country Group D:5 destinations, entities headquartered there, reexports and in-country transfers, and applications lacking the certification. Section 744.23(d) and section 748.8 receive conforming changes. Notice-and-comment is waived under ECRA section 1762.

notes: Relations and entities are populated above; section_status values are set to not_applicable only because the schema requires a value for each section. Internal inconsistency: the Supplementary Information says the lab review may be a representative sampling of a batch chosen by the lab, while the preamble bullet and paragraph (dd)(1)(ix) require review of every shipment. The 50 percent cap is measured by units shipped in the preamble bullet but by aggregate TPP in paragraph (dd)(1)(iii). NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X are named only as product examples, not as designated or addressed entities. Third-party testing labs, exporters and reviewing agencies are described by category and are not coded as named entities.
